title: Why models overfit
hook: Why can a model ace training data and fail on new cases?
explanation: Overfitting happens when a model learns noise or incidental patterns rather than transferable structure.

quiz.question: Which evaluation best detects overfitting?
quiz.explanation: Overfitting happens when a model learns noise or incidental patterns rather than transferable structure.

deeper: Compare training and validation curves; leakage can make even validation results misleading.

title: Supervised learning
hook: How does an algorithm learn from examples?
explanation: Supervised learning uses input-output pairs to learn a mapping for future predictions.

quiz.question: What does supervised learning require?
quiz.explanation: Supervised learning uses input-output pairs to learn a mapping for future predictions.

deeper: Labels may be noisy, expensive, or reflect past human bias.

title: What is a transformer?
hook: Why can language models connect distant words?
explanation: Transformers use attention mechanisms to combine information from different positions in a sequence.

quiz.question: What is a central transformer mechanism?
quiz.explanation: Transformers use attention mechanisms to combine information from different positions in a sequence.

deeper: Attention is not a guarantee of reasoning or factual accuracy.

title: The baseline challenge
hook: Your AI prototype is impressive. What should you compare it against?
explanation: A baseline is a simpler existing method that establishes whether complexity creates useful value.

quiz.question: Best first comparison?
quiz.explanation: A baseline is a simpler existing method that establishes whether complexity creates useful value.

deeper: A rules-based solution can outperform a costly model in reliability and maintenance.

title: What is retrieval augmentation?
hook: How can an LLM use documents not memorized during training?
explanation: Retrieval-augmented generation retrieves relevant documents and supplies them as context to a model.

quiz.question: What does retrieval add?
quiz.explanation: Retrieval-augmented generation retrieves relevant documents and supplies them as context to a model.

deeper: Retrieval can still surface irrelevant or outdated evidence; verify citations.

title: Precision versus recall
hook: When should a detector avoid missing cases?
explanation: Recall measures the fraction of actual positives found; precision measures the fraction of predicted positives that are correct.

quiz.question: Which metric directly measures positives found?
quiz.explanation: Recall measures the fraction of actual positives found; precision measures the fraction of predicted positives that are correct.

deeper: Threshold choices trade off false positives and false negatives.

title: Embedding spaces
hook: How can text become searchable by meaning?
explanation: Embedding models map items into vectors so similar items can be near one another in a learned space.

quiz.question: An embedding is primarily a…
quiz.explanation: Embedding models map items into vectors so similar items can be near one another in a learned space.

deeper: Similarity depends on the model, domain, and distance measure.

title: Product metrics that matter
hook: Your chatbot has many clicks. Is it helping users?
explanation: Activity metrics show usage, but outcome metrics capture whether the user goal was achieved.

quiz.question: Which is closer to user value?
quiz.explanation: Activity metrics show usage, but outcome metrics capture whether the user goal was achieved.

deeper: Pair outcome metrics with safety, retention, and user-reported experience.

title: The hallucination problem
hook: Why can a fluent answer still be false?
explanation: Generative models predict plausible outputs; fluency does not establish factual grounding.

quiz.question: Best mitigation for high-stakes claims?
quiz.explanation: Generative models predict plausible outputs; fluency does not establish factual grounding.

deeper: Use retrieval, constrained workflows, and human review as appropriate.

title: Data leakage
hook: Can a model accidentally see tomorrow’s answer today?
explanation: Data leakage occurs when training or evaluation uses information unavailable at prediction time.

quiz.question: Which is leakage?
quiz.explanation: Data leakage occurs when training or evaluation uses information unavailable at prediction time.

deeper: For longitudinal datasets, split by time and sometimes by person or site.

title: Small versus large models
hook: Is the biggest model always the best product choice?
explanation: Smaller models can be faster, cheaper, and easier to run privately, with possible quality tradeoffs.

quiz.question: Which factor belongs in model selection?
quiz.explanation: Smaller models can be faster, cheaper, and easier to run privately, with possible quality tradeoffs.

deeper: Benchmark on the real distribution and include operating costs.

title: Human-in-the-loop
hook: When should a human review an AI decision?
explanation: Human review is valuable when errors are consequential, uncertainty is high, or accountability requires oversight.

quiz.question: A useful review design should…
choices: Make uncertain cases easy to escalate
quiz.explanation: Human review is valuable when errors are consequential, uncertainty is high, or accountability requires oversight.

deeper: Reviewers need time, context, and authority to correct mistakes.

title: Experiment before scaling
hook: Your team wants to launch to everyone. What comes first?
explanation: A staged rollout can measure impact and detect failures before broad exposure.

quiz.question: Best first step?
quiz.explanation: A staged rollout can measure impact and detect failures before broad exposure.

deeper: Define stop conditions and compare outcomes to a baseline.

title: Triage app launch
hook: Your symptom checker flags too few urgent cases. What now?
explanation: In triage, missing urgent cases can be particularly harmful; assess sensitivity, severity, and clinical workflow before launch.

quiz.question: Best PM response?
quiz.explanation: In triage, missing urgent cases can be particularly harmful; assess sensitivity, severity, and clinical workflow before launch.

deeper: Escalation rules and prospective clinical evaluation are essential.

title: What is an EHR?
hook: Why is medical data so hard to combine?
explanation: Electronic health records store clinical information, but formats, coding practices, and workflows vary across organizations.

quiz.question: A key interoperability obstacle is…
quiz.explanation: Electronic health records store clinical information, but formats, coding practices, and workflows vary across organizations.

deeper: FHIR helps exchange structured healthcare information but does not solve all semantic issues.

title: The silent subgroup
hook: Your model works overall but poorly for one age group.
explanation: Aggregate metrics can hide clinically important differences between patient subgroups.

quiz.question: What should the PM request?
quiz.explanation: Aggregate metrics can hide clinically important differences between patient subgroups.

deeper: Subgroups require sufficient sample sizes and clinically meaningful outcomes.

title: Calibration matters
hook: What does a 20% risk score actually mean?
explanation: A calibrated model predicts outcomes at roughly the stated frequency among similarly scored cases.

quiz.question: A calibrated 20% risk group should have about…
quiz.explanation: A calibrated model predicts outcomes at roughly the stated frequency among similarly scored cases.

deeper: Calibration can drift across hospitals and over time.

title: The missingness clue
hook: What if a lab test is missing because the doctor was unconcerned?
explanation: Clinical data can be missing for reasons related to patient condition or clinician decisions.

quiz.question: Why does this matter?
quiz.explanation: Clinical data can be missing for reasons related to patient condition or clinician decisions.

deeper: Investigate missingness mechanisms before imputation.

title: Clinician workflow
hook: Doctors ignore your AI alert. Is accuracy the only problem?
explanation: Even accurate alerts can fail when poorly timed, hard to interpret, or disruptive to care.

quiz.question: Best discovery method?
quiz.explanation: Even accurate alerts can fail when poorly timed, hard to interpret, or disruptive to care.

deeper: Measure alert burden and downstream actions, not just clicks.

title: Software as a medical device
hook: When might software be regulated as a medical device?
explanation: Some software functions with medical purposes may fall under device oversight, depending on intended use and jurisdiction.

quiz.question: What matters especially?
quiz.explanation: Some software functions with medical purposes may fall under device oversight, depending on intended use and jurisdiction.

deeper: Regulatory classification is context-specific; seek qualified advice.

title: Consent and reuse
hook: Can patient data collected for care always be reused for AI?
explanation: Research and product reuse may require legal bases, privacy safeguards, governance, and sometimes consent.

quiz.question: What is the best default?
quiz.explanation: Research and product reuse may require legal bases, privacy safeguards, governance, and sometimes consent.

deeper: HIPAA, institutional policies, and other laws can apply differently.

title: External validation
hook: Why test at a second hospital?
explanation: A model can perform well at its development site but degrade with different populations, devices, or practices.

quiz.question: What does external validation test?
quiz.explanation: A model can perform well at its development site but degrade with different populations, devices, or practices.

deeper: Prospective validation further tests real-world workflows.

title: Choosing the outcome
hook: Your model predicts hospital readmission. What should you ask?
explanation: A prediction is only useful if a feasible intervention can improve a meaningful outcome.

quiz.question: Most useful PM question?
quiz.explanation: A prediction is only useful if a feasible intervention can improve a meaningful outcome.

deeper: Evaluate whether acting on predictions benefits patients and avoids unintended harms.

title: Clinical coding
hook: Why are ICD codes imperfect research labels?
explanation: Billing and diagnosis codes serve administrative purposes and can differ from confirmed clinical phenotypes.

quiz.question: A code should be treated as…
quiz.explanation: Billing and diagnosis codes serve administrative purposes and can differ from confirmed clinical phenotypes.

deeper: Chart review or validated phenotyping may improve labels.

title: Dataset shift
hook: Why monitor a model after deployment?
explanation: Patient populations, care pathways, and measurement practices can change, reducing performance.

quiz.question: Which monitoring is useful?
quiz.explanation: Patient populations, care pathways, and measurement practices can change, reducing performance.

deeper: Monitoring needs clear escalation and retraining governance.

title: A safer MVP
hook: You want to build an AI clinical assistant with no trial data.
explanation: A lower-risk MVP can start with administrative workflow support rather than autonomous diagnosis.

quiz.question: Best initial scope?
quiz.explanation: A lower-risk MVP can start with administrative workflow support rather than autonomous diagnosis.

deeper: Even administrative tools require privacy and accuracy controls.

title: Understanding PCOS
hook: Is PCOS only about ovarian cysts?
explanation: Polycystic ovary syndrome is a heterogeneous endocrine condition; diagnosis considers symptoms and criteria, not cysts alone.

quiz.question: Which statement is most accurate?
quiz.explanation: Polycystic ovary syndrome is a heterogeneous endocrine condition; diagnosis considers symptoms and criteria, not cysts alone.

deeper: Diagnostic criteria vary with age and clinical context.

title: Endometriosis basics
hook: Why can endometriosis be difficult to diagnose?
explanation: Endometriosis involves tissue resembling uterine lining outside the uterus; symptoms and diagnostic pathways vary.

quiz.question: Which is possible?
choices: A normal scan always rules it out
quiz.explanation: Endometriosis involves tissue resembling uterine lining outside the uterus; symptoms and diagnostic pathways vary.

deeper: Some imaging cannot detect superficial disease; consult clinical guidance.

title: The evidence gap
hook: Why should researchers analyze sex and gender?
explanation: Biological and social differences may affect exposure, symptoms, care access, and treatment response.

quiz.question: Best research practice?
quiz.explanation: Biological and social differences may affect exposure, symptoms, care access, and treatment response.

deeper: Avoid simplistic binaries when collecting relevant biological and social variables.

title: Confirmation bias
hook: Why do we notice facts that support our belief?
explanation: Confirmation bias is a tendency to seek or interpret evidence in ways that favor existing expectations.

quiz.question: Which practice helps?
quiz.explanation: Confirmation bias is a tendency to seek or interpret evidence in ways that favor existing expectations.

deeper: Precommit to what evidence would change your mind.

title: The menstrual cycle
hook: What triggers ovulation?
explanation: A surge in luteinizing hormone usually precedes ovulation during an ovulatory menstrual cycle.

quiz.question: Which hormone surges before ovulation?
quiz.explanation: A surge in luteinizing hormone usually precedes ovulation during an ovulatory menstrual cycle.

deeper: Cycle length and timing vary; calendar prediction is imperfect.

title: Fertility probabilities
hook: Why does fertility change with age?
explanation: Oocyte quantity and quality tend to decline with age, but individual fertility varies substantially.

quiz.question: Which is most accurate?
choices: Population trends do not predict an individual exactly
quiz.explanation: Oocyte quantity and quality tend to decline with age, but individual fertility varies substantially.

deeper: Fertility assessment and planning should be individualized.

title: Cognitive reappraisal
hook: Can changing interpretation change emotion?
explanation: Cognitive reappraisal involves reframing how a situation is understood and can influence emotional responses.

quiz.question: Which is reappraisal?
quiz.explanation: Cognitive reappraisal involves reframing how a situation is understood and can influence emotional responses.

deeper: Reappraisal is one strategy, not a substitute for addressing real problems.

title: Hormone variability
hook: Why is one hormone measurement sometimes misleading?
explanation: Many hormone levels fluctuate by cycle phase, time of day, medication, and physiology.

quiz.question: What helps interpretation?
quiz.explanation: Many hormone levels fluctuate by cycle phase, time of day, medication, and physiology.

deeper: Testing strategy depends on the clinical question.

title: Trial representation
hook: Why does clinical trial diversity matter?
explanation: Representation supports understanding of whether benefits and harms differ across populations.

quiz.question: Best trial design goal?
choices: Recruit populations relevant to intended users
quiz.explanation: Representation supports understanding of whether benefits and harms differ across populations.

deeper: Representation alone is insufficient without meaningful analysis.

title: Availability heuristic
hook: Why does a vivid story feel more likely than a statistic?
explanation: The availability heuristic judges likelihood partly by how easily examples come to mind.

quiz.question: What corrects this?
quiz.explanation: The availability heuristic judges likelihood partly by how easily examples come to mind.

deeper: Stories can highlight harms, but frequency needs representative evidence.

title: Period app privacy
hook: Your cycle app requests precise location for symptom tracking.
explanation: Sensitive reproductive data deserves purpose limitation, minimal collection, and transparent user control.

quiz.question: Best product decision?
quiz.explanation: Sensitive reproductive data deserves purpose limitation, minimal collection, and transparent user control.

deeper: Privacy-by-design can improve trust and reduce risk.

title: Perimenopause
hook: Does menopause happen overnight?
explanation: Perimenopause is a transition with changing menstrual patterns and symptoms before menopause.

quiz.question: Which is true?
quiz.explanation: Perimenopause is a transition with changing menstrual patterns and symptoms before menopause.

deeper: Menopause is defined retrospectively after 12 months without menstruation in appropriate contexts.

title: Correlation and stress
hook: Does an association between stress and illness prove causation?
explanation: Observational associations can reflect confounding, reverse causation, or causal effects.

quiz.question: What does correlation alone establish?
quiz.explanation: Observational associations can reflect confounding, reverse causation, or causal effects.

deeper: Longitudinal and experimental evidence can strengthen inference.

title: The trolley dilemma
hook: Can saving more people justify harming one?
explanation: The trolley problem contrasts outcome-focused and duty-focused ethical intuitions.

quiz.question: Which framework emphasizes consequences?
quiz.explanation: The trolley problem contrasts outcome-focused and duty-focused ethical intuitions.

deeper: Real decisions involve uncertainty and institutional responsibilities.

title: What can we know?
hook: Is a confident belief the same as knowledge?
explanation: Epistemology studies knowledge, justification, evidence, and the limits of belief.

quiz.question: What does epistemology study?
quiz.explanation: Epistemology studies knowledge, justification, evidence, and the limits of belief.

deeper: Confidence can be high even when evidence is weak.

title: The veil of ignorance
hook: How would you design society without knowing your place in it?
explanation: Rawls used an original-position thought experiment to explore fair principles of justice.

quiz.question: What is hidden behind the veil?
quiz.explanation: Rawls used an original-position thought experiment to explore fair principles of justice.

deeper: The thought experiment asks us to consider impartiality, not erase real differences.

title: A valid argument
hook: Can a logically valid argument have false premises?
explanation: Validity means that if premises are true, the conclusion must follow; it does not establish the premises.

quiz.question: Validity guarantees…
quiz.explanation: Validity means that if premises are true, the conclusion must follow; it does not establish the premises.

deeper: Soundness additionally requires true premises.

title: Virtue ethics
hook: What if ethics is about character rather than rules?
explanation: Virtue ethics focuses on cultivated traits such as courage, honesty, and practical wisdom.

quiz.question: Its central focus is…
quiz.explanation: Virtue ethics focuses on cultivated traits such as courage, honesty, and practical wisdom.

deeper: Virtues can conflict and require judgment in context.

title: The experience question
hook: Could two people see colors differently?
explanation: Qualia refers to subjective aspects of conscious experience, a central topic in philosophy of mind.

quiz.question: Qualia describes…
quiz.explanation: Qualia refers to subjective aspects of conscious experience, a central topic in philosophy of mind.

deeper: The explanatory gap remains philosophically contested.

title: The straw man
hook: Why is a distorted opponent easy to defeat?
explanation: A straw-man argument misrepresents a position and then attacks the weaker version.

quiz.question: Best corrective practice?
quiz.explanation: A straw-man argument misrepresents a position and then attacks the weaker version.

deeper: Steel-manning makes disagreement more productive.

title: Utilitarian tradeoffs
hook: How does utilitarianism evaluate actions?
explanation: Classical utilitarianism evaluates actions by their effects on overall well-being.

quiz.question: Its main concern is…
quiz.explanation: Classical utilitarianism evaluates actions by their effects on overall well-being.

deeper: Measuring and distributing welfare raises difficult objections.

title: The ship of Theseus
hook: If every part is replaced, is it the same ship?
explanation: The Ship of Theseus explores identity and persistence through change.

quiz.question: The puzzle concerns…
quiz.explanation: The Ship of Theseus explores identity and persistence through change.

deeper: Identity criteria differ for artifacts, organisms, and persons.

title: Freedom from or freedom to
hook: Can freedom mean more than noninterference?
explanation: Negative liberty emphasizes absence of interference; positive liberty concerns self-direction or control.

quiz.question: Negative liberty emphasizes…
quiz.explanation: Negative liberty emphasizes absence of interference; positive liberty concerns self-direction or control.

deeper: Both concepts have multiple interpretations and critics.

title: Burden of proof
hook: Who must support a surprising claim?
explanation: Claims should be supported by proportionate evidence; absence of disproof is not proof.

quiz.question: What supports a strong claim?
quiz.explanation: Claims should be supported by proportionate evidence; absence of disproof is not proof.

deeper: Extraordinary claims warrant especially careful testing.

title: Moral luck
hook: Should outcomes beyond our control change moral judgment?
explanation: Moral luck concerns how factors outside an agent’s control influence moral assessment.

quiz.question: The central tension is between…
quiz.explanation: Moral luck concerns how factors outside an agent’s control influence moral assessment.

deeper: Intention, risk, and outcome can be assessed separately.

title: Free will and determinism
hook: Can choices be free in a lawful universe?
explanation: Compatibilists argue freedom can coexist with determinism under suitable accounts of agency.

quiz.question: Compatibilism holds that…
choices: Free will and determinism may coexist
quiz.explanation: Compatibilists argue freedom can coexist with determinism under suitable accounts of agency.

deeper: Philosophers disagree about what meaningful control requires.

title: Printing and power
hook: How did movable type transform public debate?
explanation: Printing lowered the cost of reproducing texts and helped ideas spread across wider networks.

quiz.question: Its key effect was…
quiz.explanation: Printing lowered the cost of reproducing texts and helped ideas spread across wider networks.

deeper: Effects varied by region, language, and political context.

title: What is federalism?
hook: Why can two levels of government make laws?
explanation: Federal systems constitutionally divide governing authority between central and regional governments.

quiz.question: Federalism means…
quiz.explanation: Federal systems constitutionally divide governing authority between central and regional governments.

deeper: The exact division varies across countries.

title: The Silk Roads
hook: Was the Silk Road one road?
explanation: The Silk Roads were overlapping land and maritime networks carrying goods, technologies, and beliefs.

quiz.question: The Silk Roads were…
quiz.explanation: The Silk Roads were overlapping land and maritime networks carrying goods, technologies, and beliefs.

deeper: Trade also transmitted diseases and cultural practices.

title: Separation of powers
hook: Why split legislative, executive, and judicial functions?
explanation: Separation of powers aims to reduce concentrated authority through distinct institutions and checks.

quiz.question: A core goal is…
quiz.explanation: Separation of powers aims to reduce concentrated authority through distinct institutions and checks.

deeper: Institutional designs differ between parliamentary and presidential systems.

title: The Green Revolution
hook: How did crop yields rise dramatically in the twentieth century?
explanation: Improved crop varieties combined with irrigation, fertilizers, and agronomic practices boosted yields in many regions.

quiz.question: Which contributed?
quiz.explanation: Improved crop varieties combined with irrigation, fertilizers, and agronomic practices boosted yields in many regions.

deeper: Benefits came with environmental and distributional tradeoffs.

title: How a bill becomes law
hook: Does a proposed US bill become law when one chamber approves?
explanation: Ordinarily both chambers must pass the same legislation and it must complete the presidential approval or override process.

quiz.question: What is usually required?
quiz.explanation: Ordinarily both chambers must pass the same legislation and it must complete the presidential approval or override process.

deeper: Procedural exceptions and constitutional rules add complexity.

title: Why cities formed
hook: What made early dense settlements possible?
explanation: Agricultural surpluses, trade, institutions, and geography supported urban concentration in many societies.

quiz.question: A common enabling factor was…
quiz.explanation: Agricultural surpluses, trade, institutions, and geography supported urban concentration in many societies.

deeper: Urbanization emerged in different ways across regions.

title: Proportional representation
hook: How can election rules shape parties?
explanation: Proportional systems seek to allocate seats in relation to vote share, subject to thresholds and formulas.

quiz.question: A typical feature is…
quiz.explanation: Proportional systems seek to allocate seats in relation to vote share, subject to thresholds and formulas.

deeper: District magnitude and thresholds affect outcomes.

title: The Columbian exchange
hook: How did 1492 reshape global diets?
explanation: The Columbian exchange moved crops, animals, pathogens, and people between the Americas and Afro-Eurasia.

quiz.question: Which is an example?
quiz.explanation: The Columbian exchange moved crops, animals, pathogens, and people between the Americas and Afro-Eurasia.

deeper: Disease and colonial violence had devastating consequences for Indigenous peoples.

title: What is judicial review?
hook: Can courts invalidate a law?
explanation: In some constitutional systems, courts can review legislation for constitutional compatibility.

quiz.question: Judicial review tests…
quiz.explanation: In some constitutional systems, courts can review legislation for constitutional compatibility.

deeper: Scope and institutional design vary internationally.

title: The scientific revolution
hook: Was modern science born in one moment?
explanation: Early modern science developed through changing methods, institutions, instruments, and networks over centuries.

quiz.question: Which change was important?
quiz.explanation: Early modern science developed through changing methods, institutions, instruments, and networks over centuries.

deeper: The narrative of a purely European revolution overlooks global knowledge exchange.

title: Public goods
hook: Why might markets underprovide street lighting?
explanation: A pure public good is non-rival and non-excludable, making voluntary private financing difficult.

quiz.question: Which is a typical public-good feature?
quiz.explanation: A pure public good is non-rival and non-excludable, making voluntary private financing difficult.

deeper: Many real goods are mixed rather than perfectly public.

title: The census and the state
hook: Why do governments count populations?
explanation: Censuses support representation, planning, resource allocation, and research, while raising privacy questions.

quiz.question: One use of a census is…
quiz.explanation: Censuses support representation, planning, resource allocation, and research, while raising privacy questions.

deeper: Definitions and undercount can influence political outcomes.

title: Why silhouettes change
hook: How can a hemline signal an era?
explanation: Silhouettes reflect materials, technology, social norms, labor, and aesthetic movements.

quiz.question: What influences silhouettes?
quiz.explanation: Silhouettes reflect materials, technology, social norms, labor, and aesthetic movements.

deeper: Fashion histories should consider whose styles were documented.

title: The rule of thirds
hook: Why do off-center compositions often feel dynamic?
explanation: The rule of thirds is a compositional heuristic placing subjects near imagined grid lines.

quiz.question: It is best understood as…
quiz.explanation: The rule of thirds is a compositional heuristic placing subjects near imagined grid lines.

deeper: Artists often break it intentionally for expressive effect.

title: Bauhaus principles
hook: Why does modern furniture often look geometric?
explanation: Bauhaus designers explored links between art, craft, industrial production, and functional form.

quiz.question: A Bauhaus emphasis was…
quiz.explanation: Bauhaus designers explored links between art, craft, industrial production, and functional form.

deeper: The movement was diverse and not reducible to minimalism.

title: What is negative space?
hook: Can empty space be part of the subject?
explanation: Negative space is the area around and between visual elements; it shapes balance and attention.

quiz.question: Negative space refers to…
quiz.explanation: Negative space is the area around and between visual elements; it shapes balance and attention.

deeper: Intentional emptiness can improve legibility and mood.

title: The bias cut
hook: How can fabric drape without heavy tailoring?
explanation: Cutting woven fabric on the bias allows more give and fluid drape.

quiz.question: Bias cut means cutting…
quiz.explanation: Cutting woven fabric on the bias allows more give and fluid drape.

deeper: Madeleine Vionnet is strongly associated with innovative bias-cut designs.

title: Why museums label provenance
hook: Why does ownership history matter?
explanation: Provenance traces an object’s custody and can reveal authenticity, trade, or contested acquisition.

quiz.question: Provenance means…
quiz.explanation: Provenance traces an object’s custody and can reveal authenticity, trade, or contested acquisition.

deeper: Gaps in provenance warrant careful investigation, especially for cultural heritage.

title: Complementary colors
hook: Why do some color pairs create contrast?
explanation: In common color-wheel models, complementary hues sit opposite each other and can create strong visual contrast.

quiz.question: Complementary hues are…
quiz.explanation: In common color-wheel models, complementary hues sit opposite each other and can create strong visual contrast.

deeper: Color relationships depend on the color model and surrounding context.

title: Why pleats persist
hook: How can a garment expand while retaining structure?
explanation: Pleats fold fabric to create controlled volume, movement, and visual rhythm.

quiz.question: A functional role of pleats is…
quiz.explanation: Pleats fold fabric to create controlled volume, movement, and visual rhythm.

deeper: Pleating techniques vary from stitched folds to heat-set synthetic textiles.

title: Typography hierarchy
hook: How does a page tell your eye where to look?
explanation: Size, weight, spacing, and contrast organize reading order and perceived importance.

quiz.question: Which improves hierarchy?
quiz.explanation: Size, weight, spacing, and contrast organize reading order and perceived importance.

deeper: Accessibility requires sufficient contrast and readable sizes.

title: Impressionism and light
hook: Why did some painters work outdoors?
explanation: Impressionist painters explored fleeting light and perception with visible brushwork and changing color.

quiz.question: A recurring concern was…
quiz.explanation: Impressionist painters explored fleeting light and perception with visible brushwork and changing color.

deeper: Portable paint tubes supported outdoor practice, among other factors.

title: Cultural appropriation
hook: When does borrowing become exploitative?
explanation: Ethical cultural exchange depends on context, power, credit, consent, and benefit, not simply the presence of influence.

quiz.question: What matters in evaluating borrowing?
quiz.explanation: Ethical cultural exchange depends on context, power, credit, consent, and benefit, not simply the presence of influence.

deeper: Communities may disagree; listen to affected creators.

title: Why grids work
hook: How can a grid make interfaces feel calm?
explanation: Grids align elements and create predictable spatial relationships, reducing cognitive effort.

quiz.question: A grid primarily supports…
quiz.explanation: Grids align elements and create predictable spatial relationships, reducing cognitive effort.

deeper: Breaking a grid can create emphasis when done deliberately.

title: The lifecycle of a trend
hook: Why do styles return decades later?
explanation: Trends circulate through nostalgia, subcultures, designers, media, and changes in production.

quiz.question: A plausible driver of revival is…
quiz.explanation: Trends circulate through nostalgia, subcultures, designers, media, and changes in production.

deeper: Trend cycles are not perfectly periodic or universal.

title: The base-rate trap
hook: A test is 99% accurate. Does a positive mean 99% chance?
explanation: Positive predictive value also depends on prevalence and the types of test errors.

quiz.question: What else matters?
quiz.explanation: Positive predictive value also depends on prevalence and the types of test errors.

deeper: Bayes’ theorem combines prior probability with evidence.

title: Opportunity cost
hook: What do you give up when you say yes?
explanation: Opportunity cost is the value of the best alternative forgone when making a choice.

quiz.question: Opportunity cost is…
quiz.explanation: Opportunity cost is the value of the best alternative forgone when making a choice.

deeper: Time and attention also have opportunity costs.

title: Mean versus median
hook: Why can one billionaire skew an average?
explanation: The mean responds to extreme values, while the median marks the middle ordered observation.

quiz.question: Which resists extreme outliers better?
quiz.explanation: The mean responds to extreme values, while the median marks the middle ordered observation.

deeper: Choose summaries based on distribution and decision context.

title: Sunk-cost fallacy
hook: Should money already spent determine whether to continue?
explanation: Irrecoverable past costs should not drive a forward-looking decision about future costs and benefits.

quiz.question: What matters for the next decision?
quiz.explanation: Irrecoverable past costs should not drive a forward-looking decision about future costs and benefits.

deeper: Emotional attachment makes this difficult in practice.

title: Expected value
hook: Would you take a 50% chance to win $10?
explanation: Expected monetary value weights possible outcomes by their probabilities.

quiz.question: Expected winnings of 50% × $10, otherwise $0?
quiz.explanation: Expected monetary value weights possible outcomes by their probabilities.

deeper: Expected value is not the same as risk preference or guaranteed payoff.

title: Combinatorics of outfits
hook: Three shirts and four pants: how many combinations?
explanation: The multiplication principle counts independent choices by multiplying their option counts.

quiz.question: How many outfits?
quiz.explanation: The multiplication principle counts independent choices by multiplying their option counts.

deeper: Restrictions between choices can change the count.

title: Regression to the mean
hook: Why might an extreme performance be followed by an ordinary one?
explanation: When outcomes contain random variation, unusually extreme observations often move closer to the average next time.

quiz.question: Which explanation fits?
choices: Random variation around a stable tendency
quiz.explanation: When outcomes contain random variation, unusually extreme observations often move closer to the average next time.

deeper: Regression to the mean does not imply that all changes are random.

title: Explore versus exploit
hook: Should you try a new café or return to your favorite?
explanation: The exploration-exploitation tradeoff balances learning about alternatives against choosing known rewards.

quiz.question: Exploration is…
quiz.explanation: The exploration-exploitation tradeoff balances learning about alternatives against choosing known rewards.

deeper: Bandit algorithms formalize this tradeoff.

title: Independent events
hook: Does a coin remember five heads?
explanation: For independent fair flips, the next flip remains 50% heads regardless of prior outcomes.

quiz.question: Chance of heads next flip?
quiz.explanation: For independent fair flips, the next flip remains 50% heads regardless of prior outcomes.

deeper: Real-world processes may not be independent; check the assumption.

title: Price elasticity
hook: Why does a small price increase sometimes cut sales sharply?
explanation: Price elasticity of demand measures responsiveness of quantity demanded to price changes.

quiz.question: Highly elastic demand means…
quiz.explanation: Price elasticity of demand measures responsiveness of quantity demanded to price changes.

deeper: Availability of substitutes and time horizon matter.

title: Confidence intervals
hook: Does a 95% confidence interval mean a 95% chance this fixed parameter moves?
explanation: Under repeated sampling, a valid 95% interval procedure covers the fixed parameter in 95% of repetitions.

quiz.question: The 95% refers to…
quiz.explanation: Under repeated sampling, a valid 95% interval procedure covers the fixed parameter in 95% of repetitions.

deeper: Bayesian credible intervals have a different interpretation.

title: The Pareto frontier
hook: Can you improve one goal without harming another?
explanation: A Pareto-efficient option cannot improve one objective without worsening at least one other.

quiz.question: Pareto efficiency means…
choices: No free improvement on any objective
quiz.explanation: A Pareto-efficient option cannot improve one objective without worsening at least one other.

deeper: Efficiency alone does not address fairness.

title: Compounding
hook: Why does reinvested growth accelerate?
explanation: Compounding means returns can accrue on both the original amount and previous returns.

quiz.question: What produces compounding?
quiz.explanation: Compounding means returns can accrue on both the original amount and previous returns.

deeper: Real returns depend on inflation, taxes, risk, and fees.

title: Weather versus climate
hook: Can one snowy day disprove global warming?
explanation: Weather describes short-term conditions; climate describes long-term patterns and distributions.

quiz.question: Climate refers to…
quiz.explanation: Weather describes short-term conditions; climate describes long-term patterns and distributions.

deeper: Extremes can occur within a warming climate.

title: Keystone species
hook: Can one species shape an entire ecosystem?
explanation: A keystone species has an outsized effect on community structure relative to its abundance.

quiz.question: Keystone means…
quiz.explanation: A keystone species has an outsized effect on community structure relative to its abundance.

deeper: Effects depend on the ecosystem and interactions.

title: Carbon sinks
hook: Where does emitted carbon dioxide go?
explanation: Oceans and terrestrial ecosystems absorb some human CO₂ emissions, while much remains in the atmosphere.

quiz.question: Which is a carbon sink?
quiz.explanation: Oceans and terrestrial ecosystems absorb some human CO₂ emissions, while much remains in the atmosphere.

deeper: Sink strength changes with warming and ecosystem conditions.

title: Mycorrhizal partners
hook: Why do many plants cooperate with fungi?
explanation: Mycorrhizal fungi exchange nutrients and water access with plant hosts, often receiving carbon compounds.

quiz.question: The relationship often involves…
quiz.explanation: Mycorrhizal fungi exchange nutrients and water access with plant hosts, often receiving carbon compounds.

deeper: Benefits vary by species and environment.

title: Lifecycle analysis
hook: Is a reusable item always greener after one use?
explanation: Life-cycle assessment examines impacts across raw materials, production, transport, use, and disposal.

quiz.question: What should be compared?
quiz.explanation: Life-cycle assessment examines impacts across raw materials, production, transport, use, and disposal.

deeper: Results depend on usage frequency, energy sources, and assumptions.

title: Methane and CO₂
hook: Why are greenhouse gases not interchangeable?
explanation: Methane is more potent per unit mass over shorter horizons but has a shorter atmospheric lifetime than CO₂.

quiz.question: Which is accurate?
choices: They differ in lifetime and warming impact
quiz.explanation: Methane is more potent per unit mass over shorter horizons but has a shorter atmospheric lifetime than CO₂.

deeper: The time horizon changes greenhouse-gas comparisons.

title: Biodiversity insurance
hook: Why can diverse ecosystems be more resilient?
explanation: Functional diversity can support ecosystem processes when species respond differently to disturbances.

quiz.question: A potential benefit is…
quiz.explanation: Functional diversity can support ecosystem processes when species respond differently to disturbances.

deeper: Resilience is context-dependent, not automatic.

title: Why wetlands matter
hook: Are marshes just unused land?
explanation: Wetlands can store carbon, filter water, provide habitat, and buffer floods.

quiz.question: One wetland function is…
quiz.explanation: Wetlands can store carbon, filter water, provide habitat, and buffer floods.

deeper: Restoration success depends on hydrology and ecological context.

title: Albedo feedback
hook: Why does melting ice amplify warming?
explanation: Bright ice reflects sunlight; darker exposed surfaces absorb more energy, reinforcing warming.

quiz.question: Lower albedo generally means…
quiz.explanation: Bright ice reflects sunlight; darker exposed surfaces absorb more energy, reinforcing warming.

deeper: Feedback magnitude varies by region and season.

title: Invasive species
hook: Why can a newcomer disrupt an ecosystem?
explanation: Some introduced species spread and cause ecological or economic harm in environments lacking familiar controls.

quiz.question: An invasive species is typically…
choices: Non-native and harmful in its new range
quiz.explanation: Some introduced species spread and cause ecological or economic harm in environments lacking familiar controls.

deeper: Not every introduced species becomes invasive.

title: Food waste and emissions
hook: Why does wasted food affect climate?
explanation: Growing, transporting, and disposing of uneaten food uses resources and generates emissions.

quiz.question: A useful intervention is…
quiz.explanation: Growing, transporting, and disposing of uneaten food uses resources and generates emissions.

deeper: Food safety still matters when reducing waste.

title: Ocean acidification
hook: How does atmospheric CO₂ change seawater?
explanation: Dissolved CO₂ shifts seawater carbonate chemistry, lowering pH and affecting some calcifying organisms.

quiz.question: The primary driver is…
quiz.explanation: Dissolved CO₂ shifts seawater carbonate chemistry, lowering pH and affecting some calcifying organisms.

deeper: Responses differ across species and habitats.

title: Adaptation versus mitigation
hook: What is the difference between seawalls and clean energy?
explanation: Mitigation reduces emissions or enhances sinks; adaptation reduces vulnerability to climate impacts.

quiz.question: A seawall is mainly…
quiz.explanation: Mitigation reduces emissions or enhances sinks; adaptation reduces vulnerability to climate impacts.

deeper: Many climate plans need both approaches.

title: DNA as information
hook: How does a cell store inherited instructions?
explanation: DNA uses sequences of four nucleotide bases to encode biological information.

quiz.question: Which are DNA bases?
quiz.explanation: DNA uses sequences of four nucleotide bases to encode biological information.

deeper: DNA information is read and regulated through complex cellular processes.

title: Reading genomes
hook: What does DNA sequencing determine?
explanation: Sequencing identifies the order of nucleotide bases in a DNA molecule.

quiz.question: Sequencing primarily reveals…
quiz.explanation: Sequencing identifies the order of nucleotide bases in a DNA molecule.

deeper: Interpretation requires quality control and biological context.

title: Variants and risk
hook: Does a genetic variant always cause disease?
explanation: Variants can be benign, pathogenic, or uncertain; effects depend on context and evidence.

quiz.question: Which is accurate?
quiz.explanation: Variants can be benign, pathogenic, or uncertain; effects depend on context and evidence.

deeper: Clinical interpretation uses evidence frameworks and genetic counseling.

title: RNA expression
hook: Why do two cells with the same genome behave differently?
explanation: Cells express different sets and amounts of genes, shaping their functions.

quiz.question: A major difference is…
quiz.explanation: Cells express different sets and amounts of genes, shaping their functions.

deeper: Single-cell RNA sequencing profiles expression across cells.

title: Sequence alignment
hook: How do researchers compare DNA sequences?
explanation: Alignment methods arrange sequences to identify similarities, differences, and possible shared origins.

quiz.question: Alignment is used to…
quiz.explanation: Alignment methods arrange sequences to identify similarities, differences, and possible shared origins.

deeper: Scoring schemes balance matches, mismatches, and gaps.

title: Targets and validation
hook: A molecule binds a protein. Is it a medicine?
explanation: Binding is only an early clue; efficacy, selectivity, toxicity, and clinical benefit must be tested.

quiz.question: What is still needed?
quiz.explanation: Binding is only an early clue; efficacy, selectivity, toxicity, and clinical benefit must be tested.

deeper: Drug discovery has many stages and high attrition.
